title: a task may stack on another open pull request: its PR targets that branch, and when the base merges firstmate retargets and rebases it; a branch that is some open PR's base is never deleted
acceptance: Why. On 2026-09-29 the captain approved the redesign for working on other repositories (reviewed and grilled against consenlabs/tokenlon-mm-agent PR #164): external data outside the engine tree under FM_HOME, private repositories allowed, watching done by scripts at zero model cost, with visible owned Herdr dispatch retained; detached full cmux lifecycle remains deferred. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-143.json, is committed on this branch.

A task whose depends_on names a task with an open, unmerged PR may, when the project's conventions allow stacking, branch from that PR's head and open its PR against that branch (per-PR base, not the project's single base). Gates and the patch-id rule use the PR's own base.

When a base PR merges, firstmate retargets the stacked PR and rebases under project policy; later T-141 automates those mechanical steps. Review follows T-138 authoritative patch binding. Never delete a branch that remains any open PR base; retain it until last dependent retargets, then apply project deletion/retention policy.

Where stacking is off, a dependent task waits for its dependency to merge, as today. Evidence: the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Workers do not run the suites themselves. Stubs answer as the real tools do.

External project data lives only under FM_HOME/projects/<name>/{repo,worktrees,CONVENTIONS.md,tasks,design.md,state}. No private specs, worktrees, prompts, pins, evidence, mirrors or recovery data in engine state or its public tree. Private repos are accepted. Unreadable protection is unknown: require captain-confirmed project checks and policy before readiness, never infer permission or reject solely for visibility. Every GitHub operation names the project repository. Preserve self-project default and explicit-name compatibility. Never push to protected base; task-branch force-with-lease requires confirmed project policy and expected old head. Merge method, deletion, land/review/post and stacking follow CONVENTIONS.md, never hardcoded squash/delete.

Evidence: required GitHub checks and commit statuses plus six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7 on the authoritative current PR head; gate 3 is retired. Workers author feature-owned fail-first tests but run no suites. Tests stay at most 1200 lines; shared fixtures in tests/lib/ or tests/e2e/lib/, with literal helper references. Firstmate verifies CI/gates and real acceptance; a structure check cannot prove model compliance. Commit this task spec with implementation.

Use project merge/retention policy, never hardcoded squash/delete; retain any open PR base. Retarget/rebase only with authorized task-branch expected-head lease; never protected-base force push. Synchronize new authoritative head before patch comparison/gates/card. Firstmate can operate this task without T-141; autopilot integration follows.
